messages.content:
Generate a Rollup grouped by route_id. Port 1 must receive one ParcelProgress record for every input parcel, after that parcel has been included in its route totals; port 0 must receive one RouteSummary after the group.

Configuration: Component ROLLUP, groupKeyFields=route_id, inputSorted=true, groupAccumulatorMetadataId=MetaRouteAcc.

Port 0 (in):
<Metadata id="MetaParcelIn">
  <Record name="Parcel" type="delimited">
    <Field name="route_id" type="string" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="parcel_id" type="string" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="weight_kg" type="decimal" length="8" scale="3" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="surcharge" type="decimal" length="8" scale="2" nullable="true"/>
  </Record>
</Metadata>

Port 0 (out):
<Metadata id="MetaRouteSummaryOut">
  <Record name="RouteSummary" type="delimited">
    <Field name="route_id" type="string" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="parcel_count" type="integer" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="total_weight_kg" type="decimal" length="10" scale="3" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="total_surcharge" type="decimal" length="10" scale="2" nullable="false"/>
  </Record>
</Metadata>

Port 1 (out):
<Metadata id="MetaParcelProgressOut">
  <Record name="ParcelProgress" type="delimited">
    <Field name="route_id" type="string" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="parcel_id" type="string" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="parcel_seq" type="integer" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="cumulative_weight_kg" type="decimal" length="10" scale="3" nullable="false"/>
  </Record>
</Metadata>

Group accumulator metadata:
<Metadata id="MetaRouteAcc">
  <Record name="RouteAcc" type="delimited">
    <Field name="route_id" type="string"/>
    <Field name="parcel_count" type="integer"/>
    <Field name="weight_total" type="decimal" length="10" scale="3"/>
    <Field name="surcharge_total" type="decimal" length="10" scale="2"/>
    <Field name="current_parcel_id" type="string"/>
  </Record>
</Metadata>

messages.reasoning_content: ParcelProgress is post-update state, so parcel_count and weight_total change before updateGroup starts its output loop. parcel_count advances on every input, making zero a reliable first-row test for route_id. RouteAcc keeps current_parcel_id with the aggregates, so the progress callback uses one stable snapshot. Returning port 1 emits rather than terminates, so counter zero emits the detail and counter one returns SKIP; transform separately uses the same guard for its route summary.

messages.content:
Create a Rollup grouped by batch_id for a warehouse scan feed. Every scan contributes to the BatchSummary on output port 0, but output port 1 must receive ScanProgress only for scans whose scan_status is ACCEPTED.

Input ScanEvent: batch_id string non-null, scan_id string non-null, scan_status string non-null, unit_count integer non-null.
Accumulator ScanAcc: batch_id string, scan_count integer, accepted_count integer, accepted_units integer, current_scan_id string.
Output 0 BatchSummary: batch_id string non-null, scan_count integer non-null, accepted_count integer non-null, rejected_count integer non-null, accepted_units integer non-null.
Output 1 ScanProgress: batch_id string non-null, scan_id string non-null, accepted_seq integer non-null, cumulative_accepted_units integer non-null.

Input is sorted by batch_id.

messages.reasoning_content: Rejected scans affect scan_count but not accepted_count or accepted_units, so accumulation stays outside the ACCEPTED branch and rejected_count remains subtractable. updateGroup requests a progress loop only after accepted fields have changed; rejects return false but still leave final totals complete. scan_count identifies the first batch because it advances for every event. The progress callback emits only its counter-zero snapshot to port 1, while finishGroup separately permits one port-0 batch summary.

messages.content:
Write a Rollup grouped by invoice_id that uses one output port. Emit a DETAIL row for every invoice line as it is accumulated, then one SUMMARY row after the invoice. Use record_type to distinguish them.

Configuration: Component ROLLUP, groupKeyFields=invoice_id, inputSorted=true, groupAccumulatorMetadataId=MetaInvoiceAcc.

Port 0 (in):
<Metadata id="MetaInvoiceLineIn">
  <Record name="InvoiceLine" type="delimited">
    <Field name="invoice_id" type="long" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="line_id" type="long" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="line_amount" type="decimal" length="10" scale="2" nullable="false"/>
  </Record>
</Metadata>

Port 0 (out):
<Metadata id="MetaInvoiceOutput">
  <Record name="InvoiceOutput" type="delimited">
    <Field name="invoice_id" type="long" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="record_type" type="string" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="line_id" type="long" nullable="true"/>
    <Field name="line_amount" type="decimal" length="10" scale="2" nullable="true"/>
    <Field name="line_seq" type="integer" nullable="true"/>
    <Field name="running_total" type="decimal" length="12" scale="2" nullable="true"/>
    <Field name="line_count" type="integer" nullable="true"/>
    <Field name="invoice_total" type="decimal" length="12" scale="2" nullable="true"/>
  </Record>
</Metadata>

Group accumulator metadata:
<Metadata id="MetaInvoiceAcc">
  <Record name="InvoiceAcc" type="delimited">
    <Field name="invoice_id" type="long"/>
    <Field name="line_count" type="integer"/>
    <Field name="total_amount" type="decimal" length="12" scale="2"/>
    <Field name="current_line_id" type="long"/>
    <Field name="current_line_amount" type="decimal" length="10" scale="2"/>
  </Record>
</Metadata>

messages.reasoning_content: Port 0 has two shapes, so record_type selects the meaning of nullable fields and each path clears the fields owned by the other shape. line_count advances on every line and safely gates invoice_id capture. The accumulator keeps the current line with the final aggregate so each callback reads a consistent group snapshot. A port return emits instead of ending either loop, hence counter zero emits one DETAIL or one SUMMARY and the next counter returns SKIP.

Port 0 (in):
<Metadata id="MetaMachineSampleIn">

    <Field name="sample_id" type="long" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="temperature_c" type="decimal" length="6" scale="1" nullable="false"/>
  </Record>
</Metadata>

Port 0 (out):
<Metadata id="MetaMachineSummaryOut">
  <Record name="MachineSummary" type="delimited">
    <Field name="machine_id" type="string" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="sample_count" type="integer" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="average_temperature" type="decimal" length="8" scale="2" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="alert_count" type="integer" nullable="false"/>
  </Record>
</Metadata>

Port 1 (out):
<Metadata id="MetaMachineProgressOut">
  <Record name="MachineProgress" type="delimited">
    <Field name="machine_id" type="string" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="sample_id" type="long" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="sample_seq" type="integer" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="cumulative_temperature" type="decimal" length="10" scale="1" nullable="false"/>
  </Record>
</Metadata>

Port 2 (out):
<Metadata id="MetaHeatAlertOut">
  <Record name="HeatAlert" type="delimited">
    <Field name="machine_id" type="string" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="sample_id" type="long" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="temperature_c" type="decimal" length="6" scale="1" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="alert_seq" type="integer" nullable="false"/>
  </Record>
</Metadata>

Group accumulator metadata:
<Metadata id="MetaMachineAcc">
  <Record name="MachineAcc" type="delimited">
    <Field name="machine_id" type="string"/>
    <Field name="sample_count" type="integer"/>
    <Field name="temperature_total" type="decimal" length="10" scale="1"/>
    <Field name="alert_count" type="integer"/>
    <Field name="current_sample_id" type="long"/>
    <Field name="current_temperature" type="decimal" length="6" scale="1"/>

messages.reasoning_content: Every sample changes sample_count and temperature_total before its progress output, while alert_count changes only on the same >80D condition that creates an alert. Counter zero always emits the progress snapshot. Counter one emits port 2 only when current_temperature is hot, then the next invocation skips; a non-hot sample skips at counter one. Separating those callback counts allows one or two intermediate rows without reusing the final summary loop.

messages.content:
Write a Rollup grouped by session_id that outputs one SessionEvent row for every input event and deliberately produces no end-of-session summary. The full Rollup lifecycle is still required.

Input WebEvent: session_id string non-null, event_id string non-null, action string non-null.
Accumulator SessionAcc: session_id string, event_count integer, current_event_id string, current_action string.
Output 0 SessionEvent: session_id string non-null, event_id string non-null, action string non-null, event_seq integer non-null.

Input is sorted by session_id.

messages.reasoning_content: This group has no final record, so finishGroup returns false; transform remains mandatory but cannot manufacture a summary. event_count advances for every row and captures session_id only once, while current event fields preserve the snapshot that progress maps. updateGroup still returns true for each event. Port 0 is an emission, not a loop stop, so updateTransform uses its counter gate to produce exactly one SessionEvent per input.

messages.content:
Create a Rollup grouped by employee_id. Port 1 must show SubmissionProgress for every submitted claim, including rejected claims. Port 0 must show an EmployeeEligibleSummary only when the employee has at least one accepted claim.

Input ClaimSubmission: employee_id string non-null, submission_id long non-null, accepted boolean non-null, approved_amount decimal non-null.
Accumulator ClaimAcc: employee_id string, submission_count integer, accepted_count integer, accepted_total decimal, current_submission_id long, current_accepted boolean.
Output 0 EmployeeEligibleSummary: employee_id string non-null, accepted_count integer non-null, accepted_total decimal non-null.
Output 1 SubmissionProgress: employee_id string non-null, submission_id long non-null, submission_seq integer non-null, accepted boolean non-null, accepted_count_so_far integer non-null.

Input is sorted by employee_id.

messages.reasoning_content: Progress must include rejected claims, so submission_count and the current submission always update before the ACCEPTED branch. Only accepted rows raise accepted_count and accepted_total, allowing rejected_count to be derived from all submissions minus accepts. updateGroup is therefore always true, but finishGroup depends on accepted_count so an ineligible employee gets no summary. Each output loop has its own counter-zero guard, keeping every progress record and any allowed summary singular.

messages.content:
Write a Rollup grouped by account_id. Every transaction must produce one intermediate row, but credits go to port 1 and debits go to port 2. Emit one AccountSummary on port 0 after the account.

Input AccountTransaction: account_id string non-null, transaction_id long non-null, signed_amount decimal non-null. A non-negative amount is a credit; a negative amount is a debit.
Accumulator AccountAcc: account_id string, transaction_count integer, net_amount decimal, current_transaction_id long, current_amount decimal.
Output 0 AccountSummary: account_id string non-null, transaction_count integer non-null, net_amount decimal non-null.
Output 1 CreditProgress: account_id string non-null, transaction_id long non-null, transaction_seq integer non-null, credit_amount decimal non-null, net_amount_so_far decimal non-null.
Output 2 DebitProgress: account_id string non-null, transaction_id long non-null, transaction_seq integer non-null, debit_amount decimal non-null, net_amount_so_far decimal non-null.

Input is sorted by account_id.

messages.reasoning_content: Each transaction contributes to one account total before its intermediate port is selected; the sign changes the port, not whether the count or net amount advances. Zero belongs with credits by the stated non-negative rule. The output phase owns routing, so counter zero maps the snapshot to port 1 for credit or port 2 for debit. The next callback returns SKIP, while the final loop separately maps one account summary.

    <Field name="measured_count" type="integer" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="min_level" type="decimal" length="8" scale="3" nullable="false"/>

Port 1 (out):

messages.reasoning_content: input_count advances even for a null level, so it—not measured_count—safely captures station_id on the first row. A null level does not start a progress loop or participate in extrema. Initial null bounds let the first actual level establish both values; subsequent comparisons only run against real decimals. measured_count then determines both progress sequence and whether finishGroup permits a non-nullable summary, while counter guards keep each selected output loop to one row.

messages.content:
Write a Rollup grouped by campaign_id. Port 1 must receive DonationProgress for every donation. When cumulative donations first reach 10000.00 within a campaign, emit one ThresholdAlert on port 2 for the donation that crosses the threshold. Emit CampaignSummary on port 0 after every campaign.

Input Donation: campaign_id string non-null, donation_id long non-null, amount decimal non-null.
Accumulator DonationAcc: campaign_id string, donation_count integer, total_received decimal, current_donation_id long, current_amount decimal, threshold_crossed_now boolean, threshold_announced boolean.
Output 0 CampaignSummary: campaign_id string non-null, donation_count integer non-null, total_received decimal non-null, threshold_reached boolean non-null.
Output 1 DonationProgress: campaign_id string non-null, donation_id long non-null, donation_seq integer non-null, cumulative_received decimal non-null.
Output 2 ThresholdAlert: campaign_id string non-null, donation_id long non-null, amount decimal non-null, cumulative_received decimal non-null.

Input is sorted by campaign_id.

messages.reasoning_content: The alert is a threshold transition: previous_total records state before the donation, and the post-addition total establishes a crossing only from below. threshold_announced makes that transition one-way even if later donations meet the condition again. Progress always uses counter zero after the new cumulative total. Only a crossing reaches counter one for port 2, then SKIP ends that donation's update loop; transform separately emits one campaign total.

The input row does update count, total, and current parcel before returning false, but that boolean suppresses updateTransform entirely. Its populated port-1 assignments are therefore unreachable for every parcel, while finishGroup independently keeps the summary loop alive. Changing only the per-record result to true starts the already bounded detail loop; the accumulator snapshot and final summary require no other change.

Write a Rollup grouped by trip_id. Port 1 must emit one BoardingProgress record for every boarding, and port 0 must emit one TripSummary record after the trip. No group accumulator metadata is configured, so groupAccumulatorMetadataId is not set and the CTL must use VoidMetadata plus globals for all group and current-row state.

Configuration: Component ROLLUP, groupKeyFields=trip_id, inputSorted=true. No groupAccumulatorMetadataId is configured.

Port 0 (in):
<Metadata id="MetaTripBoardingIn">
  <Record name="TripBoarding" type="delimited">
    <Field name="trip_id" type="string" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="stop_sequence" type="integer" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="rider_id" type="string" nullable="false"/>
  </Record>
</Metadata>

Port 0 (out):
<Metadata id="MetaTripSummaryOut">
  <Record name="TripSummary" type="delimited">
    <Field name="trip_id" type="string" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="boarding_count" type="integer" nullable="false"/>
  </Record>
</Metadata>

Port 1 (out):
<Metadata id="MetaBoardingProgressOut">
  <Record name="BoardingProgress" type="delimited">
    <Field name="trip_id" type="string" nullable="false"/>

    <Field name="stop_sequence" type="integer" nullable="false"/>

messages.reasoning_content: VoidMetadata cannot retain group fields, so both aggregate state and current boarding snapshot need globals reset in initGroup. boardingCount advances on every input, making zero reliable for the trip-id capture and the outgoing sequence. The output phases read the globals written by updateGroup: counter zero maps one boarding to port 1 and transform's own guard maps one trip total. The VoidMetadata parameter stays in all lifecycle signatures even though no field is read from it.

messages.content:
Create a Rollup grouped by case_id. There is no group accumulator metadata configured; use VoidMetadata in the lifecycle signatures and globals for all preserved state. Emit a CheckProgress row on port 1 for every check. If the current check is blocking, emit one additional BlockAlert row on port 2. Emit one CaseSummary row on port 0 per case.

Configuration: Component ROLLUP, groupKeyFields=case_id, inputSorted=true, groupAccumulatorMetadataId is not set.

Input ComplianceCheck: case_id string non-null, check_id string non-null, risk_score decimal non-null, blocking boolean non-null.
Output 0 CaseSummary: case_id string non-null, check_count integer non-null, blocking_count integer non-null, total_risk_score decimal non-null.
Output 1 CheckProgress: case_id string non-null, check_id string non-null, check_seq integer non-null, cumulative_risk_score decimal non-null.
Output 2 BlockAlert: case_id string non-null, check_id string non-null, risk_score decimal non-null, blocking_seq integer non-null.

messages.reasoning_content: VoidMetadata holds no check state, so the key, aggregates, and current check fields are globals reinitialized at each case. checkCount advances for every row and safely gates the key. Counter zero always emits progress after cumulative risk updates; only captured currentBlocking permits counter one to emit an alert, otherwise it skips. Separate counter guards leave a single final case summary after finishGroup.

Returning port 1 emits a TransactionProgress snapshot and schedules the next update callback with a higher counter. Since the original body has no counter test or SKIP path, that same state repeats without end for one transaction. The final summary loop already has its own guard. A counter-positive SKIP is the minimal change: counter zero emits the required row, and all later calls stop.

Missing accumulator metadata does not remove the accumulator argument from a Rollup callback: the configured absence is represented by VoidMetadata. The parameterless functions therefore do not bind to the five required lifecycle signatures. The global state is otherwise appropriate because it is reset in initGroup and supplies both output phases. Add the unused VoidMetadata argument to every callback without changing the counters, mappings, or loop gates.

Count, total, and current id change for the item, then updateGroup returns false. That prevents any updateTransform invocation, so its port-1 assignments cannot emit an ItemProgress row. finishGroup independently starts the one-row summary loop. The required per-item stream is therefore absent despite valid accumulation; the explicit output requirement is breached, so one ERROR forces FAIL.

ISSUES:
  [ERROR] updateGroup() returns false for every input record, so updateTransform() is never called and port 1 receives no required ItemProgress rows. Accumulation and the final StreamSummary path still run.

SUGGESTIONS:
  - Return true from updateGroup() after updating the accumulator so each input item starts its intermediate-output loop.

VERDICT: FAIL

messages.reasoning_content: At counter zero, return 1 emits the progress snapshot and schedules updateTransform again with counter one. The body has neither a counter branch nor SKIP, so every later call re-emits the same package state. transform's summary loop is bounded independently. One input package therefore produces an unending progress stream rather than one row; the stated cardinality is broken, so one ERROR forces FAIL.

Output fields are written only in output callbacks, and transform has an independent one-row guard. No lifecycle, routing, or cardinality defect remains. Clean, PASS.
